'''Harold G. "Sonny" White''' (born October 8, 1965) is a [[mechanical engineer]], [[aerospace engineer]], and applied [[physicist]] who is known for proposing new [[Alcubierre drive]] concepts and promoting advanced [[propulsion]] projects.

== Educational ==
White obtained a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] degree in [[mechanical engineering]] from [[University of South Alabama]], an [[Master of Science|M.S.]] degree in mechanical engineering from [[Wichita State University]] in 1999,<ref>[http://www.engr.wichita.edu/hlankarani/personnel.htm Personnel page] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170426212334/http://www.engr.wichita.edu/hlankarani/personnel.htm |date=2017-04-26 }} - website of the Department of Mechanical Engineering of [[Wichita State University]]</ref> and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] degree in [[Physics]] from [[Rice University]] in 2008.<ref>[http://physics.rice.edu/Content.aspx?id=63 Graduate Study Recent Theses] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921134823/http://www.physics.rice.edu/Content.aspx?id=63 |date=2013-09-21 }} - website of the Physics and Astronomy Department of [[Rice University]]</ref><ref name="Icarus">Icarus Interstellar. [http://www.icarusinterstellar.org/team/harold-white/ "Dr. Harold 'Sonny' White"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150601090330/http://www.icarusinterstellar.org/team/harold-white/ |date=2015-06-01 }}, ''Project Icarus''.</ref>

== Alcubierre "warp" drive ==
White attracted the attention of the press when he began presenting his ideas at space conventions and publishing proposals for [[Alcubierre drive]] concepts. In 2011, he released a paper titled ''Warp Field Mechanics 101'' that outlined an updated concept of [[Miguel Alcubierre]]'s [[faster-than-light]] [[space propulsion|propulsion]] concept, including methods to prove the feasibility of the project. Alcubierre's concept had been considered infeasible because it required far more power than any viable energy source could produce. White re-calculated the Alcubierre concept and proposed that if the warp bubble around a spacecraft were shaped like a [[torus]], it would be much more energy efficient and make the concept feasible. White has stated that "warp travel" has not yet seen a "[[Chicago Pile-1]]" experiment, a reference to the very first [[nuclear reactor]], the breakthrough demonstration that paved the way for [[nuclear power]].<ref>Oswald, Ed. [http://www.extremetech.com/extreme/136408-nasa-working-on-faster-than-light-travel-says-warp-drives-are-plausible "NASA working on faster-than-light space travel, says warp drives are 'plausible'"], ''ExtremeTech''.</ref><ref name="Warp">White, Harold. [https://ntrs.nasa.gov/archive/nasa/casi.ntrs.nasa.gov/20110015936_2011016932.pdf "Warp Field Mechanics 101"], ''NASA'', Houston, TX.</ref><ref>[http://adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2003GReGr..35.2025W A Discussion of Space-Time Metric Engineering] – Digital Library for Physics and Astronomy of [[Harvard University]]</ref>

To investigate the feasibility of a warp drive, White and his team have designed a warp field [[interferometer]] test bed to demonstrate warp field phenomena. The experiments are taking place at NASA's [[Advanced Propulsion Physics Laboratory]] ("Eagleworks") at the [[Johnson Space Center]].<ref name="Warp" /> White and his team claim that this modified [[Michelson interferometer]] will detect distortion of spacetime, a warp field effect.<ref>Dvorsky, George. [http://io9.com/5963263/how-nasa-will-build-its-very-first-warp-drive "How NASA might build its very first warp drive"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130110031042/http://io9.com/5963263/how-nasa-will-build-its-very-first-warp-drive |date=2013-01-10 }}, ''io9''.</ref>

In May 2021 White and his team announced that they might have found the right configuration required to test a "chip-scale" Alcubierre drive.<ref>{{cite web

== EmDrive ==
In April 2015, the space enthusiast website [[NASASpaceFlight.com]] announced, based on a post on their site's forum by NASA Eagleworks engineer Paul March, that NASA had successfully tested their [[EM Drive]] in a hard vacuum – which would be the first time any organization has claimed such a successful test.<ref>http://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2015/04/evaluating-nasas-futuristic-em-drive/ Evaluating NASA’s Futuristic EM Drive</ref> In November, 2016, Harold White, along with other colleagues at NASA's Eagleworks program published their findings on the proposed EM Drive.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Measurement of Impulsive Thrust from a Closed Radio-Frequency Cavity in Vacuum|journal=Journal of Propulsion and Power|volume=33|issue=4|pages=830–841|doi=10.2514/1.B36120|year=2017|last1=White|first1=Harold|last2=March|first2=Paul|last3=Lawrence|first3=James|last4=Vera|first4=Jerry|last5=Sylvester|first5=Andre|last6=Brady|first6=David|last7=Bailey|first7=Paul|hdl=2060/20170000277|s2cid=126303009 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> The proposed principle of operation for this device was shown to be inconsistent with known [[laws of physics]], including [[Momentum#Conservation|conservation of momentum]] and [[conservation of energy]]. No plausible theory of operation for such drives has been proposed.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.popularmechanics.com/science/energy/a22678/em-drive-cannae-cubesat-reactionless/|title=The Impossible Propulsion Drive Is Heading to Space|date=2 September 2016|website=popularmechanics.com|accessdate=9 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sciencealert.com/the-impossible-em-drive-is-about-to-be-tested-in-space|title=The 'Impossible' EM Drive Is About to Be Tested in Space|last=Crew|first=Bec|website=sciencealert.com|date=6 September 2016 |accessdate=9 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.nationalgeographic.com/2016/11/nasa-impossible-emdrive-physics-peer-review-space-science/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161122020601/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/2016/11/nasa-impossible-emdrive-physics-peer-review-space-science/|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 22, 2016|title=NASA Team Claims 'Impossible' Space Engine Works—Get the Facts|date=21 November 2016|website=National Geographic|accessdate=9 October 2017}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NOWN0y55S88|title=How The 'Impossible Drive' Could Break Newton's Third Law|last=Seeker|date=19 November 2016|via=YouTube|accessdate=9 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://bigthink.com/paul-ratner/em-drive-the-impossible-rocket-engine-may-be-closer-to-reality|title=EM Drive, the Impossible Rocket Engine, May Be Closer to Reality|last=Ratner|first=Paul|website=bigthink.com|date=2016-09-07}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2016-12-mars-days-expert-discusses-nasa.html|title=To Mars in 70 days: Expert discusses NASA's study of paradoxical EM propulsion drive|last1=Poitras|first1=Colin|date=7 December 2016|website=Phys.org|accessdate=1 May 2018}}</ref>

In March 2021, physicists at the [[Dresden University of Technology]] published three papers claiming that all results showing thrust were false positives, explained by outside forces.<ref name="Delbert2021">{{cite web|url=https://www.popularmechanics.com/science/a35991457/emdrive-thruster-fails-tests/|accessdate=29 June 2021|title=Scientists Just Killed the EmDrive|last1=Delbert|first1=Caroline|date=31 March 2021|website=popularmechanics.com|publisher=[[Popular Mechanics]]}}</ref>

== Other works ==
White and his team are also working on several other "breakthrough [[space technology]]" projects, including a new thruster concept, another concept White claims works by utilizing effects predicted by [[quantum mechanics]]. To support this research, White's team also is developing a "micro-balance" that is capable of measuring the extremely small forces predicted to be produced by this thruster. To calibrate this balance the team plans to repeat an unsuccessful 2006 [[Woodward effect]] experiment, this time using the new micro-balance.<ref name="Eagle">{{Cite web|url=https://ntrs.nasa.gov/archive/nasa/casi.ntrs.nasa.gov/20110023492_2011024705.pdf|title=Eagleworks Laboratories: Advanced Propulsion Physics Research|date=2 December 2011|accessdate=10 January 2013|publisher=NASA}}</ref>
[[File:White-Juday Warp Field Interferometer Experiment.png|thumb|Photo of the White-Juday warp field interferometer experiment]]
Together with retired [[Johnson Space Center]] employee Richard Juday, White invented the "White-Juday warp field interferometer", which uses a [[laser]] beam, a [[beamsplitter]], and a [[charge-coupled device]] camera to detect whether a test device warps spacetime.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kakaes |first=Konstantin |date=2013-04-01 |title=Warp Factor |url=https://www.popsci.com/technology/article/2013-03/warp-factor/ |access-date=2026-06-20 |website=Popular Science |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Awards ==
In 2006, White was awarded the [[NASA Exceptional Achievement Medal]] by the [[Administrator (NASA)|NASA administrator]] for his role in getting the [[Thermal Protection System]] [[robotic arm|robotic inspection]] tools built, delivered, and certified during the [[Space Shuttle]]'s [[STS-121|return to flight]].<ref name="Icarus" /> White has also received the [[Silver Snoopy Award]] from the NASA crew office for "his actions in the discovery and disposition of critical damage to the robotic arm prior to the [[STS-121|Space Shuttle STS-121 mission]]."<ref name="Icarus" />
